item.title: Effective Error Handling in Go: Wrapping, Sentinels, and Custom Types
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: Error handling in Go is straightforward, explicit, and forces developers to deal with failure states right at the point of origin. While if err != nil is a running joke in the community, when used correctly, Go’s error handling produces robust, debuggable, and maintainable software. In my Go projects, I adhere to a set of practices that ensure errors are not just checked, but are rich with context and actionable. Let’s dive into how I handle errors effectively.
